text: Fourteen files don't read themselves. This lesson writes the one document that synthesizes them.

Lesson 15's package is fourteen files, reference material, readable in any order. This lesson's document is one narrative, read start to finish. The test: could a new hire understand the whole program from this alone?
Six sections, in order: Executive Summary, Current State, Target State, Roadmap, Governance Model, and Success Metrics.

The Executive Summary is written last but read first — the six-week DSAR, the mandate, what's been built. Current State says plainly what existed before: no owners, no checks, no declared authority over customer data.

Target State is Lesson 14's architecture: Atlas, Beacon, Comet, and Harbor feeding a governed Summit, with Lesson 9's golden Customer record and two AI pilots operating under the Lesson 13 checklist instead of outside it.

The roadmap's four phases are lessons already completed, not just planned: Foundation, Control, Operationalize, and Extend. Presenting it as a progress report, not a proposal, is itself part of the pitch.

Governance Model restates Lesson 12's federated hybrid in one paragraph. Success Metrics restates Lesson 11's five KPIs unchanged — closing with the same DSAR now carrying a ten-business-day target, measured monthly.
Next: Lesson 17 turns this written strategy into a presentation built for Dana Whitfield and the board.
